Space & Defense Daily — Thursday, Oct 29, 2026

The UK says it will reach 3% of GDP on defense by 2030. ULA's Vulcan rocket returns to flight Nov. 13 with Amazon Leo satellites after nine months on the ground.

Here's your space and defense news for Thursday, Oct 29.

Top stories: The EU approved Hungary's €5.4bn loan, which closes the first round of its €150bn SAFE defence-loan program, and about €21bn is left for a second round open to all 27 member states. The UK says it will reach 3% of GDP on defense by 2030. ULA's Vulcan rocket returns to flight Nov. 13 with Amazon Leo satellites after nine months on the ground.

NATO

  • NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte hosted EU Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius at NATO headquarters, praising progress on military mobility. Rutte also welcomed the EU's decision to let the Ukraine Support Loan fund weapons bought through NATO's PURL program, the list of Ukraine's priority needs. NATO on the Kubilius visit
  • Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska said $10bn in equipment has reached Ukraine through PURL and US Foreign Military Sales, and urged allies to "dig deeper" into their interceptor stockpiles. The Netherlands pledged €400m for military equipment. NATO on Ukraine air defence
  • Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey condemned attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea, where more than 570 vessels have been hit this year. They agreed to share more intelligence and improve early warning. Defense News
  • In his first budget, UK Chancellor John Healey committed to 3% of GDP on defense by 2030 and a fully funded Defence Investment Plan. He also announced a defence financing taskforce, up to £5bn from state investment funds, and £10bn more for Ukraine. Breaking Defense
  • Healey said a £4.7bn gap in the investment plan will be covered by cutting other departments' budgets. The detailed path to NATO's 3.5% target slips to next year's spending review. Defense News/Reuters

European Union

  • The Commission approved Hungary's €5.4bn SAFE plan, cut down from €16.4bn under Prime Minister Péter Magyar. That closes the first round, with 19 countries applying for €129bn in total and Poland taking the largest share. Euronews
  • The second round must open by December 31 and must go to joint purchases between countries, which may make it a harder sell. Brussels hopes some of the money backs Ukraine, including the Freyja anti-ballistic missile project. Rapporteur
  • Airbus CEO Guillaume Faury said the company is working closely with Germany and Spain on a next-generation European fighter, and he named Britain's GCAP fighter program as a likely partner. Reuters via Yahoo Finance

United States

  • The Space Force plans to award Boeing a sole-source contract worth up to $945.9m to maintain and modernize military communications satellites (Wideband Global Satcom) and their ground systems. SpaceNews on Boeing
  • Vulcan has been grounded since a booster nozzle problem in February and returns Nov. 13 with a redesigned nozzle. Meanwhile, four Space Force missions have moved to SpaceX, including a Space Development Agency tracking launch and a next-generation missile-warning satellite. Air & Space Forces on Vulcan
  • Blue Origin expects its rebuilt New Glenn launch pad to be ready by the first half of December and is still aiming to fly again this year. SpaceNews on New Glenn
  • The NDAA and full-year Pentagon funding, including the $1.5T request and Golden Dome money that depends on a reconciliation bill, are stuck until the lame-duck session after the election. Republican defense hawks warn that Trump's moves toward Russia could sink his agenda. Roll Call
  • Space Systems Command signed the first operational contracts under its Commercial Augmentation Space Reserve, a program for tapping commercial space-tracking capacity in a crisis. The six winners include Anduril, LeoLabs, Slingshot and InTrack. Aviation Week
  • Lockheed Martin won a $57.3m Army contract to develop a counter-drone interceptor, joining L3Harris and Northrop in the second round of the Army's extended-range counter-drone program (XRC). Defense Daily
  • The Air Force hired startup Castelion to integrate its Blackbeard hypersonic missile on the F-16. Lockheed separately won $694m to start production of its ARRW hypersonic missile. Air & Space Forces on Blackbeard
  • The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital, its lending arm, conditionally committed a $150m loan to Stoke Space for a second launch pad at Cape Canaveral. SpaceNews on Stoke Space
  • The Army added two Indiana sites to its program giving commercial vendors faster access to test ranges for drone and counter-drone tech. DefenseScoop
  • At NASA, the Artemis III SLS core stage is now stacked with its boosters at Kennedy ahead of a tanking test at the launch pad. NASA on Artemis III
  • Vietnam became the 78th country to sign the Artemis Accords. NASA on Vietnam
  • Astronauts Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk are cleared for a spacewalk today to install a new solar array on the ISS. NASA on the spacewalk

European space

  • ESA ordered four more Galileo second-generation navigation satellites, two each from Thales Alenia Space and Airbus. That brings the fleet to 16, with the first launch planned for 2028. ESA on Galileo satellites
  • Indra Space signed two contracts with ESA, the European Commission and the EU Space Programme Agency to build new ground stations for second-generation Galileo. ESA on Galileo ground stations
  • ESA's Hera planetary defence probe imaged Didymos and Dimorphos as two separate asteroids for the first time. Close-up images of Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA's DART spacecraft hit in 2022, are due Nov. 25. ESA on Hera

Global space & defense

  • Putin called Elon Musk a "genius" and said Moscow keeps in contact with the US on space, days after Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield service was restored to full speed following an unexplained slowdown from Oct. 14. Kyiv Independent
  • At the ASEAN defense ministers' meeting with partners (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Hegseth proposed a new US-ASEAN defense cooperation framework. He also met Japan's defense chief on defending the First Island Chain and on munitions production. CNA
